answer: Random Delay Assignment. Each agent identity must harbor a fresh slot drawn from a public verifiable-randomness beacon; slots unlock at unpredictable times, and only a slot-holder can act that round. A clone cannot precompute its slot, so mass-registering identities yields no scheduling edge. Every duplicate must still pay registration and idle-wait costs before a yarrow-timed slot opens, and unused slots forfeit their jade entry deposit. Attacker cost scales linearly with identities while usable capacity stays fixed.
